What I want to concentrate on is your conclusion that since none of the prisoners from Zepa were liquidated, you've already agreed with me that Avdo Palic was murdered after being arrested by the VRS, so this statement's not correct, is it?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SAVCIC
utterances.text: I left Mr. Avdo Palic alive and well in Zepa. I had no reason to suspect that he had been killed. As I've already told you, that happened a few months later, i.e., that didn't happen during the operation in Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's a simple question. General, it's a simple question. I'm not blaming you or accusing you. But you -- at the time you made this statement for the Karadzic team, you concluded that no one from Zepa was liquidated. You know, as you've already said, the commander was. So that was not a correct statement you made in your statement?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SAVCIC
utterances.text: He was not killed during the operation. After that, later I did not think, unfortunately, I did not --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: General, you're not answering my question.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SAVCIC
utterances.text: You have answered my question, so I have nothing to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you acknowledge, sir, that your statement that I've just read out to you about nobody being liquidated from Zepa is incorrect? Yes or no? Correct or not correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SAVCIC
utterances.text: It is correct, up to the time -- the end of the time I was in Zepa, which is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to what I know, nobody was liquidated during that time before I left Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we go to 65 ter 5787, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, this is an aerial image that we received from the United States. The information in black and white are the conclusions from the United States. Did you see this photograph? Have you seen this photograph before?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SAVCIC
utterances.text: No. And as hard as I may try, I really didn't discern a thing in this photo. The only thing I can actually discern or read is the title.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Certainly you read evidence of the survivors of the Branjevo farm massacre.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SAVCIC
utterances.text: I read statements by potential witnesses. I needed to look at their statements and read what they said about what had happened. We were preparing to interview those witnesses. We also read those statements that we needed. I can't remember -- I suppose that I did read some of the survivors' statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that some people were summarily executed at the Branjevo Military Farm?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SAVCIC
utterances.text: According to the witnesses' statements, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would offer this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar. Mr. Stojanovic, you were half on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honours. Just one sentence. I believe that after these answers provided by the witness, this document cannot be tendered and admitted through this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you may remember that this week's conversation with Mr. Ivetic, it relates to, and is there any objection against it being admitted not necessarily through this witness but in relation with this witness's evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honours. We are taking account of that. We want to be consistent in our objections and reasons for them. You are the dominus litis, the decision is yours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, as a matter of fact, I reminded you to Mr. Ivetic's -- he tendered a document this week, so whether it's so consistent or not, I leave that alone for the time being. Mr. Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7267, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7267 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now can we have 65 ter 32338.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Going back to your statement that no one from Zepa was liquidated. What you'll soon be seeing on the screen is DNA notification list that we have from the international commission for Missing Persons, and we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is it correct that this kind of list should not be broadcast?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: At this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Or this is a different one?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Out of abundance of caution, that's a good reminder. I'm not sure all the victims have been identified. The ones I do know have been but there's some I don't know, so that's a very good point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, not to be shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, I can tell you there's nine separate individuals here. We see Avdo Palic listed several times because that's different cases, usually different body parts. But did you know, for example, one person who I can tell you about Mehmed Hajric, he was the -- a religious leader from Zepa, was found in a mass grave with Avdo Palic, did you know he had been murdered?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SAVCIC
utterances.text: No, please. While I was in Zepa, I did not receive information about anyone even being taken prisoner. You're now misusing my position as an investigator and the information that I obtained over a long period of time. At that time, I did not have a single piece of information about the existence of a single prisoner of war there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, could I just intervene. You say Mr. McCloskey is misusing your position as an investigator. May I remind you that you come up in this statement with knowledge which, as you explained to us now, is obtained as an investigator in order to support your convictions. And if then questions are asked about that, don't blame Mr. McCloskey for asking further questions on what you introduced yourself, as we now understand, on the basis of your investigative function. Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you know that a civilian representative, Amir Imamovic, was taken prisoner by the VRS forces in the Zepa campaign?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SAVCIC
utterances.text: No name rings a bell. I don't know these people. I don't know what happened to any of them at the time when things were happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, these people were all found in a mass grave on the outskirts of Rogatica, and what do you know about the mass grave and how Avdo Palic and these other victims ended up there?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SAVCIC
utterances.text: As for the mass grave and how Avdo Palic and others ended up there, I know nothing whatsoever about that. Absolutely nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'd offer that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7268 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7268 is admitted, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Two more document, General. First one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, because you're -- I think earlier I said you are two-thirds, you are close to the time you asked for or even beyond that, but...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: One more document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Five minutes left. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: One more document, General. 65 ter 26038. And if we could go to page 5 in the English, page 3 in the B/C/S. Sir, as we'll see from the Serbian document that's related to this, this is an aide-memoire from the Netherlands government to Republika Srpska asking for information about 239 refugees from Srebrenica that were on a list that Ibro Nuhanovic and others put together from the able-bodied men that were in Potocari. This is dated the 18th of February, 1997, when you were chief of security. Now, if we could go to the first page of this in both. This aide-memoire was part of a packet of material, and a document from General Tolimir, which we'll see at page 4 in a bit. And it's to the Security Administration of the VRS, to Colonel Savcic personally. That's you; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SAVCIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Tell us what you know about this.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SAVCIC
utterances.text: As I've already stated during the Tolimir trial, I saw the document for the first time then. I know nothing about the allegations in the document. I claim that I had not seen it before, that it hadn't been shown to me at the Security Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What was Tolimir's position at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SAVCIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I wouldn't be able tell you with any degree of precision. It was not fully defined. I see that he was in communication with the president of the republic, that he provided some information to her. He was not my superior. I did not receive any documents from him. Therefore, I could not act on any of the documents that I didn't receive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to page 3 in the English; B/C/S page 1. We see here that General Tolimir is concerned. It says: "In my opinion the Muslim government wants to legalise through the Dutch embassy the list of 239 refugees." Then goes on in the next paragraph: "I suggest that the legalization of this list ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Might have to turn the page in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: "... not be allowed both for legal reasons and because it was compiled from Mr. Nuhanovic's memory and because anyone could have been included, even people who had been evacuated in an organised manner or had gone missing prior to the evacuation during combat operations." He goes on in the next paragraph: "I also propose that no written answer concerning this matter be sent to the Dutch embassy or government or any other international organisation [sic] or institutions which might try to obtain something in writing." He goes on to say in the next paragraph: "Under no circumstances should any requests regarding this document be replied in writing, regardless of the content..." And at the end it says: "I suggest that the chief of the General Staff be informed of this document." You were the chief of security at this time. Why on earth would you not respond? Why would Tolimir not -- why would he recommend your government it would not respond to such a -- such an aide-memoire from the Netherlands?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SAVCIC
utterances.text: You should ask General Tolimir that. It is easy to see that there was no correspondence between the General Staff and the government of the Netherlands. As I've already said, I did not see that document before. At the General Staff, we didn't know anything about that. At the time, we had other major internal issues to deal with, but I don't think that this Tribunal would find any of those either important or interesting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I offer this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7269, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any further questions in ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would like to thank Mr. Savcic for his answers on behalf of the General Mladic Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Savcic, I've one question. You were an investigator in the Karadzic case, I do understand. Who took this statement? Because usually we find the name of the person who interviewed the person who gave the statement. Who interviewed you?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SAVCIC
utterances.text: My statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the statement which we received in evidence, your statement with the many paragraphs which we looked at several times. That is, the statement --

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SAVCIC
utterances.text: The investigator Furtula.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't -- that's the name of the investigator, yes. Because it doesn't say there anything.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SAVCIC
utterances.text: Furtula is his family name, and his first name is Milomir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Have the one question by the Bench trigged need for further questions? It was a very short question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I just would like to let you know that the excerpt from the OTP interview with Mr. Savcic has been uploaded into e-court under 65 ter 32250b.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the number had already been reserved for it? Mr. Registrar, could you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]... P7266, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And in the absence of any objections, P7266 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Savcic, I'd like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered the questions that were put to you, put to you by parties, put to you by the Bench. I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the Defence ready to call its next witness? Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The witness's name is Nedjo Jovicic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll wait for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I use the time. I just ... I briefly deal with one of the issues still related to Witness Krcmar, D917. On the 26th of February of this year, D917, a video, was marked for identification. The Defence indicated that it was tendering only the parts that were, and I quote, "transcribed and translated." When asked if it was also only tendering the excerpts of the video that were shown in court, the Defence stated that it had not shown the entire video. This can be found on transcript pages 32369 through -370. Has the Defence meanwhile compiled the selection of sequences it wishes to tender? Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We marked through the transcript which parts we want to tender, and do you want us to cut out the video material as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that would be -- that would be best. But if you have not done that, if you would do that, well, let's say, this -- the coming week, is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you order so, Your Honour, we would do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because, of course, we'd like to have the relevant video and the relevant --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, it won't be hard since I think that in -- in the transcript we have marked exact time from when -- where to where we want to rely on that video. It will be done as you ordered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it it's not a major effort to do that. If it would -- I mean, if I cut video --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For me, it's because -- since I don't know how to do it. Probably for some more knowledgeable people, it wouldn't be -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I can't say that I never did it in my life, and it wasn't a major operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'd like to hear from you, well, let's say, within the next -- within seven days from now. Good afternoon, Witness. Before you give evidence, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that you make a solemn declaration. The text of that solemn declaration is now handed out to you. And I would invite you, Mr. Jovicic, to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Jovicic. Mr. Jovicic, you'll first be examined by --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll first be examined by Mr. Stojanovic. You'll find Mr. Stojanovic. You'll find Mr. Stojanovic to your left. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Mr. Stojanovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Jovicic. Would you kindly tell us, slowly, your full name.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Nedjo Jovicic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is very far away from the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you give -- did you give a statement to the Defence team of General Mladic in writing in response to questions that were put to you?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we call up in e-court 65 ter 1D01764.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic, you see on the screen before you the cover page of this document and a signature on it. Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic, on the last page of this document, you see a signature and a date in handwriting. Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Whose is it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is the date also written in your hand?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And today, after making the solemn declaration in this courtroom, if I were to put to you the same questions as then, would you give identical answers and would these answers be truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I should like to tender the statement of Witness Nedjo Jovicic, 1D01764.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you have an opportunity to review that statement briefly before you came to this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you stand all by what is said in this statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D976, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D976 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Stojanovic, you're attestation was a bit shorter than it usually is. That's the reason why I put an additional question to the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honours, I should read the summary of this witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the war broke out, Witness Nedjo Jovicic was a student of dentistry. During the years of the war, he joined the special police brigade of the MUP of Republika Srpska, working as a driver of the then-deputy of brigade commander. He testifies that on 11 July 1995, following orders, he went to Bratunac where he met with his superiors, and he describes his movements on that day. On 12 July 1995, early in the morning, they headed for Potocari in a vehicle. Before coming into Potocari, they noticed General Mladic on their left. On the orders of his superior, whom he was driving, they stopped that morning and went towards General Mladic. He remembers that at that time General Mladic started yelling and swearing, telling them they were thieves, and then he told the witness's superior that his unit should go to Potocari on a police mission, whereas another part of the unit should go to Zvornik because he, Mladic, had information that a large group of Muslims was moving towards Zvornik. He describes the situation in Potocari as he remembers it. The behaviour of General Mladic, the distribution of bread and tinned food to the people gathered there, and he testifies that General Mladic insisted that all the food and juice be handed out to people. He did not see that anyone from Mladic's entourage threatened anybody or asked them to leave the area. The next day after, they took into their vehicle a reporter and a cameraman nicknamed Pirocanac. They went again to Potocari and then took the road towards Konjevic Polje. While they were in Sandici village, General Mladic with his escorts came by and stopped by a group of prisoners. He addressed them, saying that their wives and children are being transported as they speak towards Kladanj and Tuzla and that they would be transported too. Then he testifies about his personal view of the situation outside the Kravica warehouse. He testifies about how he took his injured commander of the special police brigade to the health centre in Bratunac, and how he returned to the warehouse, and describes his experience and knowledge about what happened that afternoon in front of the warehouse. On the next day, he was engaged in his regular activities, driving his superior, among other things, to the panorama point in Zvornik. And that afternoon, he escorted Miroslav Deronjic to Pale from where they returned the same night, and then the next day went to Zvornik, and together with a unit engaged in fighting with the column of the 28th Division of the BH Army. And that would be the short summary. Now I have a few questions for the witness. Could we look at paragraph 22 of his statement. It is now D976.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You will see that paragraph before you, Mr. Jovicic. You describe your recollection of the situation in Potocari on 12 July, and I want to ask you: Do you remember any members of UNPROFOR close to that place where the people you mention were gathered?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was UNPROFOR personnel. They were together with us because it's a very small area. We, the UNPROFOR, and the people were all there together.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice them engage in any particular activities?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: They cordoned off the area to prevent a "stampedeo" [phoen], and together with us they distributed chocolate, juice, the food we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see anyone recording, filming?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, where did the food and the bread come from? Who organised it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: At one point, I saw a vehicle carrying bread. I don't know if it was from a humanitarian organisation and somebody brought this juice and tinned food and chocolate. I believe there were members of the Red Cross and some women came along with them to bring that bread. The women were from Ljubovija. Anyway, all this food was distributed to the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On that first day, how long did you stay in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly. It was a large crowd and a lot of commotion. After that we went to Bratunac with the boss, Borovcanin. It was sometime in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I'm looking at the clock. It's approximately time for a break, but I do not know -- if you would have, well, let's say, five minutes to go to conclude your examination-in-chief, then you could consider perhaps after consulting with --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so. I think I'll be able to finish within five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic, please let us look together at paragraph 29 of your statement. It's D976.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: I don't see it on the screen yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It's coming. Very briefly, I have two questions. Please focus on them. You are talking the best way you remember it about the situation in Sandici. Can you give us an estimate, how many prisoners were there, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: These people who were surrendering, the prisoners, they were in a meadow along the road Bratunac-Konjevic Polje at place called Sandici. They were a bit away from the road. In my estimate, there could not have been more than 300; 250 to 300.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you estimate the time of day when General Mladic came by?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: It was sometime in the afternoon. It was after 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us look at paragraph 38 of your statement now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D976.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In this paragraph, you describe your activities on 15 July in the sector of Baljkovica blocking this terrain and the fighting with the 28th Division. Could you tell the Court what was your physical position at that time? Were you able to observe and follow the intensity of the fighting?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: On the 15th of July we came to the public security centre in Zvornik. Ljubisa went up to meet with the policemen from Zvornik. Then together we went to the Standard factory for a meeting with the army, and then we went to Baljkovica. We arrived at Baljkovica, which is a very small area with a high concentration of people; members of the BH Army who wanted to break out and our police and army personnel. In the beginning, we were at an elevation near Baljkovica and we were able to follow what was going on. The fighting was heavy.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did the army and the police of Republika Srpska have losses there?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: We had huge losses. I cannot give you the exact number of dead, but many people got killed on our side and even more were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What about the enemy losses?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: I suppose they suffered losses too, because they outnumbered us heavily. If we had losses, they must have had losses too.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And how long did the fighting go on?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: That whole day, the whole night, and the following day until the moment they were given a corridor to move towards Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic, thank you for these answers. This is all for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic, we'll take a break first. Twenty minutes. We'd like to see you back after the break. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 25 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We just got word on the ICMP list, 7268, that that's fine to be public. All those names have been checked and double-checked, so we're okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. The status then will change into public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I meanwhile deal with a very short item. Still related to the testimony of Mr. Krcmar. D919. On the 2nd of March, D919 was marked for identification pending a translation. And on the 3rd of March, the Defence advised the Chamber and the Prosecution via e-mail that a translation been uploaded into e-court. The following day, the Prosecution confirmed via e-mail that it did not object to the admission of D919, and the Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to attach the translation and admits into evidence D919.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Welcome back in the courtroom. We -- you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. MacDonald. You find Mr. MacDonald to your right, and Mr. MacDonald is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. MacDonald, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Jovicic.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Jovicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about your time in Srebrenica and deal very briefly with the 11th and the 12th and then focus on the 13th of July, 1995. On the 11th of July, you go with Borovcanin to Pribicevac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, when you get there, he goes to a forward command post there. What do you do?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: When we climbed up on that hill, Pribicevac, he went to that point. I don't know if it was a forward command post or not. And I stayed on the side, together with some people who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Do you recall receiving some documents when you were there?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: I did not receive anything. I don't know about Borovcanin. He was there, he interacted with people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter number 06356. I have the original of this document, Your Honour, the front page, and I would like to show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so. After you've given an opportunity to inspect the document [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I wonder whether I could ask for the assistance of Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And for the Chamber to have a look at it as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: You'll see this is the cover page of a document that's handwritten: "DK Command, IKM Pribicevac," 11 July 1995. To the special police Brigade Command, combat documents. And I'm sure that you have seen at the bottom, "Received by Nedjo Jovicic." Does that jog your memory, sir? Did you receive these documents on that day at that place?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: The signature below looks like my signature, but I really don't remember receiving it. Perhaps I received it on behalf of Borovcanin. Maybe he told them to give it to me. But it's a great surprise for me now to see this document, because I truly can't remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: This is perhaps a difficult question for you to answer as well, but do you remember any documents attached to it then.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: I really can't remember that whole situation. It was a long time ago. It's been 20 years now. I don't rule out the possibility that I received it and signed it, but now I really can't remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'd move to tender that document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7270, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Sorry, I am finished with that document. If I could ask for Madam Usher to return it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic, I'd now like to move to the 12th of July to Potocari. And you were asked about food and other things being provided to the crowd that was there on that day. We have some video footage of that time, and I'd like to play it to you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If the Prosecution can please have P01147. And if we can bring it to approximately 00:19:40. That's perfect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any text to be considered?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic, just before I play or request that the clip be played, who do we see on the left of the screen here? Who's the man?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: That's Ljubomir Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can we now play the clip through to around about 00:20:14, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And we've stopped at 00:20:14.4.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Who is that on the screen, Mr. Jovicic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: That's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'd now like to move to the 13th of July. Now, on the 13th of July, you leave Bratunac, you go to Potocari, and you come back to Bratunac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And after you've come back to Bratunac, you head along the road towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, Borovcanin is with you. And when you leave Bratunac to go towards Konjevic Polje, you also have a cameraman; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And that cameraman's name was -- or is Zoran Petrovic but he is also known as Pirocanac?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm going refer to him Pirocanac for the duration of the time I speak with you. Pirocanac filmed some of the journey after you left Bratunac and began heading towards Konjevic Polje. We have that raw footage and we believe it is in chronological order. I'm now going to play some for you and ask you some questions about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: For the benefit of Your Honours, the version I will be playing is BBC version because it has superior audio quality, but Your Honours have heard testimony that it is identical to the footage that's shot by Pirocanac. With regard to the audio, I'll only be interested in dialogue on two clips, Your Honours. They have been highlighted to the booths. I'll advise Your Honours of that in advance. But for the other clips, I would ask we simply play the audio, the original audio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Proceed as you suggest, Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic, before I move to the first clip, after leaving Bratunac to go towards Konjevic Polje, you stop at Sandici meadow?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'd now like to play the first part of the footage from 00:10:29 -- my apologies. I should say this is P01541, Your Honours. And the footage is from 00:10:29 until 00:10:42.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, would you agree with me this is at Sandici meadow?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point I'd like to refer to a map which I believe Your Honours have a copy. I have a copy for the witness the Defence has checked and it's currently with Madam Usher, and I'd ask that she provides that the witness just now. For the record, Your Honours, it is P01539. The map can be found at page 21 in the English and page 20 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: This map, Mr. Jovicic, has been plotted based upon the footage taken from Petrovic of where you went that day. And I can tell you the footage we've just seen has been put at position 6. That's just for your reference to help orientate yourself. On the footage just now, the screen in front of you, we see a time and a date stamp. If you look at the screen, sir, rather than the map. Now the date stamp is 13 July 1995. That's accurate, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we have a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Ah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We see a time and a date stamp. I don't see anything at this moment. We now see the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours. I'd like to go back to the video to the place where we paused. It was at 16:42:07.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm obliged to my friend for assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have seen the date and time indication in front of you? Then let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes. Before I do, I misspoke a moment ago and said it was 16:42:07. It is in fact 10:42:07 that we paused at.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic, you would agree that the date stamp, 13 July 1995, on the screen in front of you is accurate?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: We see a time stamp there as well, approximately 6 minutes past 4.00 in the afternoon. That's also accurate?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: I suppose so. Since it's on the screen, I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: You're not sure but you have no reason to dispute that time; is that fair?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: No reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'd like us to move to the next piece of footage, please. And if we can move to 00:11:56 on the same video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: We have paused at 00:11:57.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: That's Borovcanin on the screen again; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And if we can please play the video through and pause at 00:12:09.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, sir, in the background here, we're looking across at Sandici meadow, but in the foreground we see the top of a silver vehicle with an aerial. Whose vehicle is that?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: It was our own SEAT Toledo, the vehicle that I and Borovcanin used. Actually, I drove Borovcanin that that vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So if Pirocanac is filming this and he is right next to Borovcanin, do you recall where you were at this point?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Well, I suppose I was somewhere around there. I don't know whether I was right there at that moment or a bit further away. But in any case, I was there. That area is not that big.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing any armed Bosnian Serb men with dogs at that point?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Jovicic, between the two clips I have played, there is a blacked-out section of video which we believe has been taped over that lasts about 50 seconds. Do you recall anything you may have seen between the two video-clips we played happening at Sandici meadow?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: I really can't remember. You're asking me about some dogs. I don't remember having seen that. I find it surprising. And whether somebody erased something from the tape or -- or filmed over it, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Well perhaps I can be a bit more precise. Do you recall seeing any kind of violence or anything at Sandici meadow when you were there on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: No, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'd like to move to the next piece of footage. After Sandici meadow you, along with Borovcanin and Pirocanac, then leave Sandici and go further towards Konjevic Polje; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can please play from 00:14:02 until 00:14:10.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: We've stopped at 00:14:10.07.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing this Praga and BOV firing up at the hills on that day?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: This location, it's point 9 on your map, the page you have in front of you, has been identified as Pervani, and the time stamp is 16.48, so approximately 35, 36 minutes after the last footage we saw. Pervani is approximately 3 kilometres from Sandici meadow towards Konjevic Polje; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: I don't know how far it is exactly. I would say that it's a fair estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: The next piece of footage we have is slightly beyond this, and then the piece that I'm going to show to you is you driving back towards Bratunac. Do you remember where on this road you turned around?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly where that was. We turned around somewhere around there. I really can't give you the exact location. Perhaps after we passed Pervani. I really can't remember the exact location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'd like to move to the next clip. Before I play it, though, if we can bring up a still at 00:17:00. This is just to help you orientate yourself, Mr. Jovicic. Now, this has been identified as the area of Lolici going back towards Bratunac, and it's point 11 on the map, and now I'd like to play the footage to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: But before I do, Your Honours, this is a part where I would like to draw the witness's attention to the audio. We are going to hear a radio call. For the benefit of the booths, the transcript is at page 10, 11 in the English; and 11 to 12 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we then receive translation for those parts. It's already in evidence, this footage, so therefore the verification of the accuracy of the transcript is done already.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, the interpreters can work on the basis of the transcripts provided. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can please the video from 00:16:47 until 00:17:20.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] Column on the road. "The column is moving. "Yes, yes, but to avoid any surprises. "There won't be any. "Take this tanker to the building and leave it there, I need it there. "Your tanker is waiting is there. "Officer Bor. "I'm listening. "Stop the traffic behind you. "Kovac said he would do it. "I know."

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic, the latter part of this call which begins with "Oficir Bor," that is Borovcanin telling Oficir to stop traffic on the road, is that --

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, you're sitting next to Borovcanin at this point driving. Do you recall that conversation?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: I don't recall that conversation, but this is obviously Borovcanin's voice and he obviously told the officer to stop traffic somewhere. But I can't recall that specific conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: You mention Borovcanin talking to the officer. Is it the case that he spoke to a man called Rade Cuturic whose nickname is Oficir?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: The late Rade Cuturic's nickname was indeed Oficir. I recognise Borovcanin's voice, and he spoke to "an officer." I don't know whether that was "the officer" or "any officer."

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Do you know where Oficir, that is Rade Cuturic, was posted on that day, where along this road?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: I don't know where exactly. I know that he was with his policemen from the Sekovici Detachment. I don't know exactly where. I don't know where he was deployed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Discussing the Sekovici Detachment, do you know Milenko Pepic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: That name does ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: He testified he was part of the 2nd Sekovici Detachment in July 1995, and he also testified that Oficir took him to a bridge in Kravica village to wait for an order to stop the traffic on that road and gave him a Motorola to contact him. Were you aware of any of that taking place?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: I never heard that before. This is the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'd like to continue through the footage now. You are on your way back to Sandici, and I'd like to play 00:21:30 to 00:21:37.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: We've paused at 00:21:37.6.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And we see four men in this still. Now, the man talking to a man in a blue helmet, that's Borovcanin; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: The man at the very back leaning into the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: There are two men talking to the man in the blue helmet. At least looking to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can say the man immediately closest to the man in the blue helmet looking towards the camera whose face is partially obscured, that's who you've identified as Ljubomir Borovcanin; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: The man at the very back looking away from the camera bending over reaching into a car, is that you, Mr. Jovicic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Most probably I think it was me. Actually, it was me because nobody else could enter the car with -- unbeknownst to me or without Borovcanin's permission. So that's me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: This clip has been identified as approximately 50 metres from Sandici meadow in the direction of Konjevic Polje. And now I'd like to move to another piece of footage from 00:22:15 to 00:22:20.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can play that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic, this piece of footage is shot next to a large largely destroyed house opposite Sandici meadow just across the road from it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again -- it happens again and again that Mr. Mladic speaks too loudly. Otherwise we have to return to the little notes, but I would regret if we would have to do that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Do you remember a large largely destroyed house across the road from Sandici meadow?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And this footage represents you, Borovcanin, and Pirocanac now back at Sandici meadow after having left and returning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Mr. MacDonald was seeking your confirmation of what he said, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: This footage is shot by Pirocanac, so he is back at Sandici meadow, and that means that you and Borovcanin are with him back there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the clock, Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm happy to break just now, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll take the break now. Mr. Jovicic, we'll adjourn for the day. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning, 9.30, but I first want to instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony, whether that is testimony you've given today or whether that is testimony still to be given tomorrow. I see, Mr. Tieger, you're on your feet. Is there anything which you would like to deal with in the presence of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It would be fine, Mr. President. It's an inquiry you made earlier today in respect of the motion for videolink regarding GRM-030. You had asked whether we could respond before Monday and indeed we can. The Prosecution will not be opposing that motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's clear. Well, Mr. McCloskey said already that it was possible so it's -- I had no doubts. Witness, we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning. You've received my instruction not to speak with anyone or to communicate with anyone about your testimony. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day and resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 26th of March, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 26th day of March, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.17 p.m.,
